title: The effect of ChatGPT on students’ learning performance, learning perception, and higher-order thinking: insights from a meta-analysis
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT improves student learning outcomes and under what conditions its effects are strongest. The authors note that prior studies reported mixed findings about ChatGPT’s value in education, so they conducted a meta-analysis to estimate its overall effects on learning performance, learning perception, and higher-order thinking, and to test whether those effects vary by grade level, course type, learning model, duration, role of ChatGPT, and application area.

The study synthesized 51 experimental and quasi-experimental studies published between November 2022 and February 2025, yielding 72 independent effect sizes. The included studies covered primary, secondary, and college settings, but the final moderator analyses for higher-order thinking were based only on college-level studies. ChatGPT was used in a variety of instructional roles, including intelligent tutor, intelligent partner, and intelligent learning tool, across STEM, language/writing, and skills/competencies courses, often in personalized, problem-based, project-based, contextual, or reflective learning arrangements.

Overall, the meta-analysis found that ChatGPT had a large positive effect on learning performance and moderate positive effects on learning perception and higher-order thinking. For learning performance, the strongest effects appeared in skills-and-competencies courses, problem-based learning, and interventions lasting 4–8 weeks. For learning perception, duration was the only significant moderator, with longer interventions producing larger effects. For higher-order thinking, effects varied by course type and were strongest when ChatGPT functioned as an intelligent tutor. The authors conclude that ChatGPT can support learning when used in well-structured ways, but they also emphasize the need for appropriate scaffolds and more evidence from broader contexts.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed meta-analysis of 51 experimental/quasi-experimental studies with explicit inclusion criteria, effect-size computation, heterogeneity tests, publication-bias checks, and sensitivity analyses. The design is high credibility for causal synthesis, though most primary studies are varied in context and the paper does not focus on K-12 subgroup differences.
impact_tier_rationale: The synthesized effects are medium-to-large and consistently positive for learning performance (g=0.867), perception (g=0.456), and higher-order thinking (g=0.457). However, the evidence is not specifically K-12 subgroup-focused and much of the sample is college-based, so the impact for the user’s target K-12 subgroups is only indirectly supported.

interventions.use_case: Meta-analysis of ChatGPT use as an intelligent tutor, intelligent partner, and intelligent learning tool for student learning tasks, including tutoring, assessment/feedback, and personalized recommendations across K-12 and college contexts.

finding.finding_summary: Across 44 independent effects, ChatGPT had a large positive effect on learning performance (Hedges g=0.867, 95% CI 0.683 to 1.052). The meta-analysis included 51 studies and found the strongest performance gains in skills/competencies development and problem-based learning contexts, with effects moderated by course type, learning model, and duration.
finding.measure: Learning performance tests/exams; post-test standardized mean differences
finding.study_size: n=varied across 44 independent effects from 51 studies

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT showed a moderately positive effect on learning perception across 19 independent effects (g=0.456, 95% CI 0.287 to 0.625). The paper reports that longer interventions were associated with larger gains in perception, with the >8 week subgroup showing the strongest effect (g=1.054).

ChatGPT had a moderately positive effect on higher-order thinking across 9 independent effects (g=0.457, 95% CI 0.255 to 0.650). The strongest effects were reported when ChatGPT acted as an intelligent tutor (g=0.945), and effects varied by course type, with STEM-related courses showing the largest gains.
finding.measure: Higher-order thinking scales/questionnaires (e.g., critical/creative thinking dimensions)
